# Home
*Diabetes Summer Camp for Children & Teens*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/
## Welcome to Setebaid Services!
## Diabetes Education & Support at Summer Camp
Setebaid Services® is a not-for-profit organization providing diabetes education and support **summer camp** programs for **children and teens with diabetes** and their families.
Our primary goal is to enhance the quality of life for youth living with diabetes and their families, and provide them with **enjoyable summer camp experiences** which are shared with their peers.
Our programs aim to promote a **healthy lifestyle** while fostering a community of support from families who face similar challenges on a daily basis.
**[Request Info](https://setebaidservices.org/contact-us/request-info/)**
**Fun, Unique & Educational Diabetes Summer Camps:**
Several **diabetes summer camps** take a fun, unique, and hands-on approach to diabetes education in a support group setting. The education is intentional and integrated so well into the programs that **the participants don’t realize they are learning**!
Those who attend our summer camps return home with a new sense of **independence** and **understanding**.
**The bonus**: They have gained new friends who share living with diabetes and understand their life’s challenges!
**We look forward to seeing you soon at camp!**
*[Embedded video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VqXLCz9T65A&t=4s]*

# Typical Day at Camp
*A Typical Day at Summer Camp*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/a-typical-day-at-camp/
While each summer camp has a specific schedule, this typical day schedule is very close to what camper should expect to see.
We adjust the schedule based upon the camp, special events, and age of the campers.
Our **youngest campers** will go to bed the earliest and teens will have additional night activities.
Our **teen campers** will have longer to sleep in the morning, which research shows fits their biological clocks better.
The typical schedule is based upon our 8-12 years-old camper schedule.
7 AM Wake Up, Bathroom time, Blood Glucose Monitoring (BGM) and Time to meet with the Medical and Dietary Team
8 AM Breakfast
9:15 AM Cabin Clean Up, also known as “Yuckie Duties”
9:45 AM First Activity Period (Arts & Crafts, Archery, Boating, etc.)
10:45 AM Second Activity Period (Arts & Crafts, Archery, Boating, etc.)
11:45 AM BGM at the last activity area or cabins
12 Noon Lunch in Dining Hall
12:45 PM Third Activity period
1:30 PM Fourth Activity period
2:15 PM Rest Time
3:15 PM Snack
3:30 PM Pool for Free Swimming
4:45 PM Quiet Time, Pump Changing Time, Shower Time, etc.
5:15 PM BGM, Meet with Medical and Dietary Team
5:45 PM Dinner in Dining Hall
6:30 PM Cabin Preparation Time for Evening Activity
7:30 PM Evening Activity
9:00 PM BGM, Meet with Medical and Dietary Team
9:15 PM Snack, Brush Teeth, Cabin Time
9:45 PM Lights Out

# Events
*These Events Support Camp Setebaid & Its Mission*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/events/
### Join us to and show your support for Camp Setebaid and the Harrisburg Diabetic Youth Camp:
## Dahlias for Diabetes - You Give. We Give. August 14-22, 2026
[Dahlias for Diabetes](http://dahliasfordiabetes.com) is back! In 2025, Lilly Huber and her Mom, LeeAnn, raised approximately $1,600 for our not-for-profit organization, Setebaid Services, by selling fresh-cut flowers. This year, they're blooming again with the goal of raising $3,000 to support our mission to "turn diabetes around" and make a difference for children living with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D). From Aug 14 - Aug 22, your $20+ donation will be matched with a donated dahlia bouquet sent to a nonprofit in their area, spreading joy while helping youth living with T1D. Donors will receive a fundraiser update sharing where all the bouquets were delivered.
## Dueling Pianos with the Flying Ivories October 16, 2026, from 7-10 pm Fero Vinyards & Winery
Join us for a fun evening of interactive entertainment that blends music, comedy, and audience participation!
The event features [The Flying Ivories](https://www.flyingivories.com/) in the [Fero Vineyards & Winery](https://www.ferovineyards.com/) pavilion. Doors will open at 6 PM, with a meal provided by [Catering for You](https://cateringforyou.co/) at 6:15. Fero's fabulous selection of wines will be available for purchase all evening.
[Tickets](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1998799873227?aff=oddtdtcreator) are $60 per person or reserve a table that seats 8 for $400. All tickets include the meal. **Must be 21 years old or older to attend. ID required.**
Song requests will be available for a donation. There will also be a basket raffle.
All proceeds from this fundraiser help support the Setebaid Services, Inc., Campership Fund for Camp Setebaid and the Harrisburg Diabetic Youth Camp. Limited seating is available. For more information call 570-524-9090 or email info@setebaidservices.org.

# About
*Diabetes Education at Summer Camp*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/about/
Setebaid Services, a not-for-profit organization, forges partnerships with healthcare providers and diabetes educators to operate **diabetes summer camps** and other social support programs for their pediatric patients with diabetes.
## Education is the Key for Children & Teens Living with Diabetes
Our organization focuses on the patients, children and teens with diabetes, and recognizes **education** is the key to improved health for these youth.
This prevention model is a catalyst to learning, infusing **medical professionals’** expertise, with c**ertified diabetes educators** and **professional teachers**’ educational psychology to improve how **we teach youth to manage their diabetes**.
Setebaid Services **summer camp programs** serve as the method to teach the youth; our volunteers remain key to improving the lives of the children and families we serve.
### Training Knowledgeable Health Care Professionals
Setebaid also recognizes we need healthcare professionals knowledgeable in diabetes care to help future generations. Using a similar philosophy of hands-on learning, the organization uses its programs to educate future healthcare providers.
Those who have trained through the Setebaid educational program have included trainees with:
- A.I. DuPont Hospital for Children, Department of Pediatric Endocrinology
- The Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) Diabetes Center - East Carolina University Department of Pediatric Endocrinology - Geisinger Department of Pediatric Endocrinology
- Hunter College Nutrition Program - Lancaster General Hospital Family Practice Program - The Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania
- Marist College (Physician Assistant Program) - Marywood University Department of Nutrition and Dietetics - Neumann University Nurse Practitioner Program - New York University Department of Nutrition - PennState University Children’s Hospital Department of Endocrinology - University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine

# Our Staff
*Summer Camp Leadership*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/about/camp-leadership/
Every staff member who volunteers at camp fulfills an **essential role** in serving our campers with Type 1 Diabetes. Whatever responsibility they might have, camp leadership is essential in ensuring, a **safe**, **educational**, and **fun week** for our summer campers.
**Counselor:** Counselors work **directly with campers** and ensure the campers have the **best week** of their summer.
**Senior Counselor:** Senior Counselors have previous experience at camp and ensure the cabin **works together as a team** throughout their week at camp.
**Head Counselor:** Head Counselors are **experienced professionals** who coach Senior Counselors, Counselors, and campers as needed.
**Counselor-In-Training Director:** The Counselor-In-Training (CIT) Director mentors a select group of 16 & 17 year old campers through **additional camp programs** meant to build maturity & leadership.
**Camp Director:** The Camp Director works hand-in-hand with all other camp staff members (counselors, medical team, dietitians, etc) to make sure **summer camp is a fun & safe experience for everybody.**
If you would like to **volunteer** for any of these opportunities, please fill out a “[Staff Interest Form](https://setebaidservices.org/volunteer-camp-staff/staff-interest-form/)” found under [Volunteer Camp Staff](https://setebaidservices.org/volunteer-camp-staff/)!

# Mission & History
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/about/history-goals/
## The Setebaid® Summer Camp Approach
Our summer camp programs take a fun, unique, and hands-on approach to diabetes education.
The “home away from home” element of our camps facilitates valuable **real-life learning experiences**.
Those who attend our programs return home with a sense of **independence** and **understanding**, and **new friends who share their same life experiences**!
## Philosophy
Setebaid Services believes diversity, equity, and inclusion are at the heart of a thriving organization. As a social services agency building a community to support those affected by diabetes, we implore everyone in our community to share in this philosophy. We empower positive change in the world when everyone in our community from all backgrounds, beliefs, identities, and abilities, are valued and actively engaged in Setebaid camps and programs. Together, we endeavor to create an expansive and inclusive community open to diversity of ideas, experiences, perspectives, and voices. By respecting others beliefs, we share the love which is required to make our camps, programs, and community prosperous.
In addition, Setebaid Services is committed to the health, safety, and welfare of its campers and staff. We take seriously our responsibility to manage risks and continually analyze campers’ well-being and safety, without compromising the purpose of any camping program: to experience the out-of-doors, to build community, to develop camper skills, to have an enjoyable recreational experience, and to foster and develop friendships. The organization understands hands-on education is an effective teaching style.
## History & Mission
Setebaid Services® was named by our beloved campers! Believing together we can “**turn diabetes around**,” our name is diabetes spelled backwards. Our programs began in 1977 and Setebaid Services was officially incorporated in 1998.
## Making a Difference for Children living with Type 1 Diabetes
Since our beginning, we have made it our mission to **make a difference** in each of our camper’s lives.
We have grown tremendously over the years and continue to do so with the help of our campers and their families, alumni, health professional partners, and donors.
We strive to show children living with diabetes they can lead **normal, healthy lives**. For one week during the summer, they are surrounded by other campers their age who face the same daily struggles of managing diabetes.
In addition, many of the Camp Counselors and other **camp staff also have diabetes**!
Our goal is to provide a **safe and fun atmosphere** for children of all ages while teaching them **healthy habits** as they manage their diabetes.
We operate in a **family atmosphere** and consistently welcome new members to our Setebaid Family.
### Forging Partnerships with Diabetes Educators
Setebaid Services’ objective is to forge partnerships with healthcare providers and diabetes educators to operate diabetes summer camps for their pediatric patients with diabetes. The organization focuses on the individuals, **children and teens living with diabetes**, and recognizes education is the key to improved health for them.
This **prevention model** is a catalyst to learning, infusing medical professionals’ expertise, with certified diabetes educators and professional teachers’ educational psychology to improve how we teach youth to manage their diabetes.
Setebaid Services programs serve as the method to teach the youth; our volunteers remain key to improving the lives of the children and families we serve.
### Mission
Setebaid Services is a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization to enhance the quality of life for people with diabetes and their families by:
1. Educating people with diabetes and their families to accept diabetes and maintain good glycemic control while living normal, healthy lives. 2. Educating healthcare professionals and training future healthcare professionals to effectively manage and treat people with diabetes. 3. Encouraging diabetes research.
Our **diabetes summer camps for children and teens** meet our mission by educating campers and their families effective ways to manage diabetes while having fun.
- The diabetes management skills learned are more effective because they are “**caught not taught**”. - We do not lecture campers or their families, but rather use “**teachable moments**” throughout the day where we can coach individuals as they manage their own care.
### Training Future Healthcare Professionals
Our diabetes camps meet the second part of our mission by **training future healthcare professionals**. Outstanding institutions partner with us to offer their patients a **quality diabetes camp for children and teens**.
**Prestigious pediatric endocrinology faculty** actively participate in our diabetes summer camps; these are the same experts other physicians turn to when they seek expertise for their patients. These partnerships have included
- A.I. DuPont Hospital for Children
- The Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) Diabetes Center - East Carolina University Department of Pediatric Endocrinology - Geisinger Department of Pediatric Endocrinology
- Hunter College Department of Nutrition - Lancaster General Hospital Family Practice Program - The Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania - Marywood University Department of Nutrition and Dietetics - Neumann University Nurse Practitioner Program - New York University Department of Nutrition - PennState University Children’s Hospital Department of Endocrinology - University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine
## Summer Camp Goals
Setebaid Services’ summer camps are transformational by…
- Enabling children with diabetes to meet others living with diabetes - Easing parents’ worries associated with raising a child living with diabetes - Providing a healthy, enjoyable camp experience for children with diabetes - Fostering independence by increasing diabetes management skills - Teaching children living with diabetes is not a restrictive lifestyle - Enabling children to interact with healthcare professionals in a non-clinical setting - Training future healthcare professionals effective diabetes management skills in a practical and effective hands-on learning environment
## Effective Diabetes Summer Camps
Join us at ***diabetes summer camps*** where the education is intentional and effective, and where the campers don’t realize they're learning.
Setebaid summer camps are **leaders in the diabetes camping industry** with over **40 years** of positive experience and exceptional outcomes!

# Message from our Director
*Welcome to Setebaid Services!*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/about/message-from-our-director/
We’re truly delighted you’re considering becoming part of the Setebaid Family. Since our founding, we’ve been committed to empowering youth living with diabetes and their families through education, support, and an extraordinary camp experience.
Setebaid’s flagship summer camp, **Camp Setebaid®**, began in 1978 through the collaboration of a pediatric endocrinologist, a dietitian, and a teacher. Together, they created a unique model where medical knowledge, nutrition, and education blended seamlessly to provide one of the best diabetes education programs available.
In 1998, Setebaid Services® was incorporated to carry this mission forward and expand it. That same year, the **Harrisburg Diabetic Youth Camp**—founded in 1978—joined our growing family, further enriching our network and legacy.
Our philosophy is simple but powerful; we use a **team approach to teaching about Diabetes Care.** Today, we continue to use this model to teach children and teens how to manage their diabetes. Backed by university research and—most importantly—stories from campers and their families, we know our programs don’t just educate; they **transform lives.**
Our dedicated faculty come from top universities and training facilities. They serve as expert mentors to campers while also training future healthcare professionals—doctors, nurse practitioners, nurses, and dietitians alike. And remarkably, our entire team is made up of volunteers—people who are not only deeply passionate about what they do but also living examples of thriving with diabetes.
What makes Setebaid truly special is the sense of **community and family** we foster. Campers learn from our team, and our team learns just as much from them. Together, we laugh, grow, support one another, and build memories that last a lifetime.
We hope you’ll join us on this journey—to educate, to support, and to celebrate life while living with diabetes. At Setebaid Services, we’re not just a program—we’re a family.
Hoping to see you soon…
Mark Moyer, MBA, MHA Executive Director Setebaid Services, Inc.

# Alumni
*Setebaid Alumni*
Old URL: https://setebaidservices.org/alumni/
Alumni are anyone (e.g. campers, staff, or participants) who have attended one of our summer camps or programs:
- The Badger Diabetes Youth Camp in Spencer, NY - Camp Needles in the Pines in Blounts Creek, NC - Camp Setebaid® held at Camp Louise in Shickshinny, PA - Camp Setebaid® at Mount Luther in Mifflinburg, PA - Camp Setebaid® at Swatara in Bethel, PA - The Diabetes Family Weekend in Danville, PA - Camp Setebaid® at Camp Victory in Millville, PA - The Diabetes Family Weekend at Split Rock Resort in Lake Harmony, PA - The Harrisburg Diabetic Youth Camp in Millville, PA or Bethel, PA
Attending a Setebaid camp makes you a **part of our family**!
Setebaid alumni **continue to meet** even after camp is over. **Events** are held throughout the year to keep the connections you make at our programs strong. Many of our alumni even **return as counselors**!
And…**remember to connect with us** on social media like Facebook and Twitter!
### Give the Gift of Setebaid so Others May Benefit Like You Did!
Would you like to **help others** through a Setebaid program as you were helped?
As a former camper, you can make a **huge difference** in the lives of the children currently attending our camps. We’d **love** to have you volunteer or become a member of our staff!
Visit our Volunteer Camp Staff pages to see what is available and learn how you can get involved.
**We look forward to having you back!**
